name: Fault-Tolerant Reallocation and Return
summary: A UAV fails mid-mission: declare the fault, reallocate coverage to the rest of the fleet, recover safely.
objective: When {fault_uav} declares a {fault_type} fault at t = {fault_at_s} s, reallocate its share of {critical_task} to the remaining fleet so that critical coverage stays above {critical_coverage_pct} %, and recover {fault_uav} to {rtb_zone} without any other conflict.
brief: During {critical_task} the UAV {fault_uav} will suffer a {fault_type} fault at about t = {fault_at_s} s. The mission still requires at least {critical_coverage_pct} % of the critical work. Reallocate the faulted UAV's share within 90 s of the fault declaration, keep the remaining work safe, and bring {fault_uav} back to {rtb_zone} without breaching the geofence. Report what was dropped.

parameters.name: critical_task
parameters.desc: Mission element that must stay above the coverage floor

parameters.name: critical_coverage_pct
parameters.desc: Coverage that must be kept after the fault

preconditions: fault injection enabled in the scenario

actions: re-split the faulted UAV's remaining work
report dropped work and residual risk

checkpoints.name: Fault declaration
checkpoints.metric: time from injection to acknowledged fault report

checkpoints.name: Reallocation
checkpoints.metric: time to publish new assignments and coverage kept afterwards

checkpoints.name: Recovery report
checkpoints.metric: work dropped and resume plan submitted
checkpoints.target: report contains dropped tasks and a resume plan

failure_conditions: faulted UAV crashes or lands outside {rtb_zone}
constraints: faulted UAV may not continue work after the declaration
no new task may be started after t = 600 s
grading: global checkpoint pass rate; checkpoint weights sum to 100
